The kinds of tokens.

  • Enum Constant Summary

    Enum Constants
    Enum Constant
    Description
    COMMENT
    A line or block comment.
    DECIMAL
    A decimal number with digits on both sides of the point, e.g., 19.99.
    DEDENT
    The end of a block of indented lines, an empty span: the closing brace that Layout inserts.
    DOUBLE
    A double, a decimal number with an exponent, e.g., 1.2e2 or 1.0e-2, as the compiler prints a double literal.
    EOF
    The end of the input, an empty span after the last character.
    ERROR
    Text that is not a token, e.g., an unexpected character or an unterminated string.
    ESCAPE
    An escape to a backend, [alloy| ... |] or [choco| ... |], set aside like a comment (ClaferLexer).
    INDENT
    The start of a block of indented lines, an empty span: the opening brace that Layout inserts.
    INT
    A natural number, e.g., 16.
    KEYWORD
    A reserved word of the full language, e.g., abstract, some or X (ClaferLexer): it cannot name a clafer.
    SEPARATOR
    The separator that Layout inserts between two lines at the same indentation, an empty span, so that, e.g., a group cardinality at the start of a line is not the cardinality of the clafer on the line before.
    STRING
    A string literal with its quotes and escapes as written, e.g., "a\"b"; see Lexer.unescape(String).
    SYMBOL
    An operator or punctuation, e.g., ->>, .. or a brace.
    WORD
    A name or a keyword, e.g., c0_cost, abstract, int: keywords are recognized by the parser where they are expected, so a clafer may be named like one.

  • Enum Constant Details

    • WORD

      public static final TokenKind WORD
      A name or a keyword, e.g., c0_cost, abstract, int: keywords are recognized by the parser where they are expected, so a clafer may be named like one.

    • INT

      public static final TokenKind INT
      A natural number, e.g., 16. A sign is a separate -.

    • DECIMAL

      public static final TokenKind DECIMAL
      A decimal number with digits on both sides of the point, e.g., 19.99.

    • DOUBLE

      public static final TokenKind DOUBLE
      A double, a decimal number with an exponent, e.g., 1.2e2 or 1.0e-2, as the compiler prints a double literal.

    • STRING

      public static final TokenKind STRING
      A string literal with its quotes and escapes as written, e.g., "a\"b"; see Lexer.unescape(String).

    • SYMBOL

      public static final TokenKind SYMBOL
      An operator or punctuation, e.g., ->>, .. or a brace.

    • COMMENT

      public static final TokenKind COMMENT
      A line or block comment. Comments are set aside, not passed to the parser.

    • ERROR

      public static final TokenKind ERROR
      Text that is not a token, e.g., an unexpected character or an unterminated string. The lexer reports a diagnostic for it and goes on.

    • KEYWORD

      public static final TokenKind KEYWORD
      A reserved word of the full language, e.g., abstract, some or X (ClaferLexer): it cannot name a clafer. The explicit languages have none (WORD).

    • ESCAPE

      public static final TokenKind ESCAPE
      An escape to a backend, [alloy| ... |] or [choco| ... |], set aside like a comment (ClaferLexer).

    • INDENT

      public static final TokenKind INDENT
      The start of a block of indented lines, an empty span: the opening brace that Layout inserts.

    • DEDENT

      public static final TokenKind DEDENT
      The end of a block of indented lines, an empty span: the closing brace that Layout inserts.

    • SEPARATOR

      public static final TokenKind SEPARATOR
      The separator that Layout inserts between two lines at the same indentation, an empty span, so that, e.g., a group cardinality at the start of a line is not the cardinality of the clafer on the line before.

    • EOF

      public static final TokenKind EOF
      The end of the input, an empty span after the last character.
